record.paper_title: Exploring Progressions: A Collection of Problems
record.context_brief: Link between AP and HP data
record.original_question: Assume α, β, and γ are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression, and β, γ, and δ are nonzero consecutive terms of a harmonic progression. Prove that α/β = γ/δ.

evidence.quote: If the numbers α, β, γ are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression and the nonzero numbers β, γ, δ are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression, show that α/β = γ/δ.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Three real numbers x, y, z are said to be consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression if 2y = x + z. Three nonzero real numbers x, y, z are said to be consecutive terms of a harmonic progression if their reciprocals 1/x, 1/y, 1/z form an arithmetic progression, equivalently 2/y = 1/x + 1/z.

Let α, β, γ, δ be real numbers with β, γ, δ nonzero. Suppose that α, β, γ are consecutive terms of an arithmetic progression and that β, γ, δ are consecutive terms of a harmonic progression. Prove that
   α/β = γ/δ.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a standard elementary exercise. From 2β = α+γ and 2βδ = γ(β+δ), one obtains αδ = (2β−γ)δ = 2βδ − γδ = γβ, hence α/β = γ/δ. The result is fully solved by direct algebraic manipulation.

status_evidence.title: Standard AP/HP identity
status_evidence.snippet: Definitions of arithmetic and harmonic progressions used to derive identities of this kind.
status_evidence.claim: The identity follows directly from the defining relations 2β = α+γ and 2/γ = 1/β + 1/δ.
